transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Tom Bennett (Novara Head of MLOps), Leah Ortiz (Novara VP Eng), Samir Patel (Novara FinOps), Riya Kapoor (Novara Security)

Summary: quick renewal check-in to confirm renewal terms, discuss expansion to additional regions and upgraded capacity, review security asks (KMS/SOC2) and plan next steps for benchmark POC and contract amendment.

Topics: renewal timeline, committed capacity options, additional regions (EU/APAC), security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs), benchmark/POC plan, pricing and contract amendment

Transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Tom: yeah, loud and clear, thanks Alyssa.
[00:05] Leah: hi all. quick heads up we only have about 40 minutes.
[00:07] Alyssa: perfect, we'll be concise. main goals today: confirm renewal timing, discuss your capacity increase request and adding eu and ap regions, and make sure security questions are covered. Marco will cover performance and benchmarks.
[00:20] Marco: hey, quick context — last quarter you were running on our hosted tier with ~200 concurrency, average p95 lat around 240ms for the chat flows, and you started some Dedicated pods for heavy batch embeddings. correct?
[00:30] Tom: yep that's right. embeddings heavy at night. we hit a few throttles in feb during the marketing campaign.
[00:36] Samir: that caused some overages so finance wants a clearer committed option with predictable unit costs.
[00:41] Alyssa: understood. we proposed a reserved capacity plan in the renewal which includes dedicated GPU pool options and optional burst capacity. wanted to get your feedback on the sizing numbers — you asked for a 2x capacity bump and two new regions, right?
[00:49] Leah: correct — eu-west-1 first, and then ap-southeast-1 later in Q3.
[00:54] Marco: technically that's straightforward. the main considerations are: provisioning lead time for Dedicated nodes in the region, model variant placement (some of your models are quantized, some not), and KV cache locality — if you want low p95 across regions we'll colocate caches.
[01:06] Riya: on security, quick question — we need to ensure BYOK KMS integration and audit logs for token-level access, also SOC2 scope needs to be explicitly covered for the Dedicated environment.
[01:14] Priya: we can support customer-managed KMS (BYOK/HSM) in Private and in Dedicated via our KMS integrations; audit logs are available with the enterprise add-on and we can include retention options. we'll share the controls matrix.
[01:23] Riya: okay, please share the controls matrix, last time some of the fields were a bit off — e.g., they listed "KV cache" as a managed service but our procurement flagged it as unclear.
[01:33] Marco: yeah, sometimes the transcriber in the docs says KV cache as K V cash in the auto doc, sorry about the typo. We'll clarify in the runbook.
[01:40] Tom: on SLA, we need 99.9% availability for our production endpoints; is that included with the Dedicated commit?
[01:46] Alyssa: Dedicated includes SLA tiers. 99.9% is available on the production tier with reserved capacity and monitoring. For the EU region there might be a 4-6 week provisioning horizon depending on demand, but we can prioritize your fleet once the contract is signed.
[01:58] Samir: lead time is fine as long as cost is predictable. can you outline pricing for monthly vs annual commits? and how burst usage is billed?
[02:07] Alyssa: yes — we'll send two committed options: a monthly reserved pool and an annual discounted commit. Burst is metered at a higher per-hour rate and we cap monthly burst spend if you opt in. I'll include exact numbers in the follow-up.
[02:19] Leah: also want to confirm model placement: we want embeddings in eu for EU user data residency, and maybe for chat flow keep US for now. can Redwood route by region and enforce model variants?
[02:28] Marco: absolutely; routing policies can be per-route. you can pin model versions, and we can do auto-fallback to a compatible quantized variant if the exact model isn't available in a region. small caveat: slight latency trade-off for fallback model, we'll note that in the playbook.
[02:41] Riya: for KMS — does the Dedicated option let us use our AWS KMS keys inside the VPC?
[02:46] Marco: yes, for Dedicated and Private you can supply customer-managed keys; we also support HSM in private deployments. encryption-in-transit and at-rest are standard.
[02:54] Tom: ok, about the benchmark — we'd like Redwood to run a run of our staging corpus and validate p95 and cost-per-1k tokens. how long does that usually take?
[03:02] Marco: typical benchmark with your corpus is 2 hours of wall time to run and then ~24 hours to produce the detailed report with token breakdowns. but we can pre-provision nodes and get you initial results within the day of the run.
[03:12] Samir: we want to cap cost during the benchmark so the bill doesn't surprise us. can Redwood run it under a trial bucket?
[03:18] Priya: yes — we'll run benchmarks under a test allocation tied to your deal, won't hit your prod billing. we'll also provide per-token and per-route cost estimates.
[03:26] Leah: great. timeline wise — our renewal auto-renews end of April, we need signed amendment before 2027-04-20 to lock rates.
[03:33] Alyssa: got it. we'll target sending the amendment by 4/7 and if you sign by 4/20 we'll lock current pricing levels.
[03:39] Riya: one more security question — audit log retention minimum, can we set 1 year? and is access via SIEM supported?
[03:46] Marco: yes, retention is configurable up to multi-year via the enterprise add-on. SIEM integration via syslog/S3 is supported; we'll include the integration steps in the doc.
[03:54] Tom: competitors — just so you know, BigModel Inc and MegaCloud AI both pitched reserved endpoints. BigModel was cheaper but their latency numbers were worse. we ran a small smoke test.
[04:03] Alyssa: thanks for sharing that context; our focus is minimizing regressions in quality while bringing unit cost down. in particular, Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization profiles that fit your workload.
[04:14] Samir: if we commit to an annual pool, can we convert unused hours to credits?
[04:18] Priya: generally we have rollover credits for annual committed plans up to a limit; I'll include exact rollover policy in the contract.
[04:24] Leah: okay let's recap next steps before we run out of time.
[04:27] Alyssa: recap: Alyssa will send the updated pricing and contract amendment by 2027-04-07. Marco will schedule the benchmark and share the runbook and pre-provision test nodes by 2027-04-09. Priya will share the onboarding checklist and controls matrix link (sec-docs.redwood.ai/novara). Novara (Riya) will provide KMS details and SOC2 gaps by 2027-04-08. Novara (Samir) to confirm budget approver by 2027-04-10.
[04:46] Tom: sounds good. one ask — can you include a simple chart of expected cost per 1M tokens for the monthly vs annual commit? that's the one thing finance will look at.
[04:54] Alyssa: yes will include that in the follow-up spreadsheet.
[04:57] Leah: thanks all. anything else?
[04:59] Marco: just a note — during the benchmark we'll test both quantized and fp16 model runs to show tradeoffs.
[05:05] Riya: thanks everyone.
[05:07] Alyssa: great — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites. thanks for the time.

End of transcript.

References/shared artifacts noted in call:
- Renewal proposal doc (link sent in chat)
- Security controls matrix: sec-docs.redwood.ai/novara (will be updated)
- Benchmark runbook (to be shared by Marco)
- Pricing spreadsheet (will be attached by Alyssa)
